subject: MATHEMATICS
title: Philippine Money Market
objective: Read and compare schematic peso and centavo amounts.
introduction: Milo is at the market with ₱20! Help him read peso and centavo amounts.

vocabulary.definition: Coins and bills used to buy things, like pesos and centavos.
To tell which amount is greater, less, or equal.
The main unit of money in the Philippines, written with the ₱ sign.

items.prompt: Which statement about money is true?

options.text: One peso equals 100 centavos. Use original tokens, not reproduced banknotes.

items.explanation: 1 peso = 100 centavos, so ₱1.00 = 100 centavos. 50 centavos is half of one peso, not ₱50.
₱5.00 means 5 pesos. 50 centavos is half of one peso, written ₱0.50.

items.prompt: Which money statement is NOT true?
items.explanation: 50 centavos is half a peso, or ₱0.50 — not ₱50. 100 centavos make ₱1.00.

items.prompt: How many centavos equal one peso?
items.explanation: One peso is divided into 100 centavos.

options.text: Using real-looking counterfeit notes is okay

items.explanation: ₱12.50 has 50 centavos and ₱12.05 has only 5 centavos, so ₱12.50 > ₱12.05. Real money, never counterfeit notes, must be used.
